why: Rebuild the integer both ways with shifts: little-endian puts byte i at bit offset 8*i, big-endian at 8*(n-1-i). Compare each reconstruction to value.
hints: Endianness is just which end of the array holds the least significant byte.
little = OR of bytes[i] << (8*i); big = OR of bytes[i] << (8*(n-1-i)).
Check little first (so palindromic byte arrays and single bytes return 'little'), then big, else 'neither'. O(n).
pitfalls: If both match, the answer is 'little', so test it first.
A value too large for n bytes simply matches neither reconstruction; no special case needed if you build from the bytes.
Shift by 8 bits per byte, not 1.
